In GLSL it is written like this:

mat2 rot(float a){ float c = cos(a), s = sin(a); return mat2(c, s, -s, c); }

Mind the order: GLSL builds matrices by columns, not by rows. That is why the -s appears third and not second. It is the silly mistake everybody makes once.

And once defined, it is used by multiplying: p = rot(0.5) * p;
